Referral Note (primary care)

Mr. Ellison, a 31-year-old man, is referred for psychiatric evaluation and treatment planning. Over the past six years he has had three psychiatric hospitalizations, and previous diagnoses have included bipolar disorder and schizophrenia. He describes recurrent periods of depressed mood and periods of elevated mood, and he reports ongoing auditory hallucinations. He stopped all of his medications approximately four months ago. He is unemployed and lives with his parents. No significant medical history. Denies alcohol and illicit substance use. Referred for diagnostic clarification and treatment recommendations.

Behavioral Observations (on arrival)

Appearance: Casually dressed; adequately groomed. Over-ear headphones around his neck.

Behavior: Cooperative but guarded. Glances toward the corner of the room at intervals during the interview.

Speech: Mildly slowed.

Mood / Affect: Mood "okay." Affect blunted.

Thought / Perception: Thought processes mildly disorganized. Reports ongoing auditory hallucinations.

Cognition / Insight: Alert. Insight poor; judgment impaired.
